question.text:
The following virtual-to-physical address translations are observed for a process. All addresses are $32$ bits long.

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Virtual address} & \text{Physical address} \\
\hline
\texttt{0x00080AF0} & \texttt{0x00101AF0} \\
\texttt{0x00002224} & \texttt{0x00083224} \\
\texttt{0x00073234} & \texttt{0x00183234}
\end{array}
\]

Which page size is consistent with all three translations?

  1. Only $64$ KB
     
  2. Only $4$ KB
     
  3. Both $64$ KB and $4$ KB
     
  4. Neither $64$ KB nor $4$ KB
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
A processor experiences a TLB miss while translating an address using a two-level page table.

What is the number of main-memory accesses required only for the page-table lookup?

Do not include the final access to the requested instruction or data.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Which of the following statements about multi-level page tables are correct?

  1. A multi-level page table may consume more pages than a linear page table for some address-space usage patterns.
     
  2. Page-table memory is generally easier to allocate because lower-level tables are divided into separate page-sized chunks.
     
  3. Without a TLB hit, a multi-level page-table lookup generally requires more lookup accesses than a linear page table.
     
  4. Systems with larger virtual-address spaces commonly use more page-table levels.
     
  5. A TLB reduces the amount of memory occupied by the multi-level page table.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
A system has:

  • $15$-bit virtual addresses
     
  • Page size $=32$ bytes
     
  • A two-level page table
     
  • One-byte PDEs and PTEs
     
  • Entry format: one valid bit followed by a $7$-bit physical-frame number
     
  • Page-directory base register $PDBR=73$
     

The required physical-memory pages contain:

Page $6:$

0a 1c 01 14 0b 1a 19 0a
0a 1a 0c 14 02 0c 1c 0c
15 04 0e 13 17 11 08 05
08 07 04 13 0f 1d 0f 1e

Page $73:$

a2 d2 97 96 d9 7f 87 b4
b7 f2 f4 82 bf 7f be 93
e8 9d 99 9e f1 7f 7f b0
d8 da eb b1 81 c3 c2 f6

Page $114:$

7f 7f 7f 7f 82 7f 7f 7f
7f 7f 7f 7f 99 7f 7f 7f
7f 7f 7f 86 7f 7f 7f 7f
7f 7f 8f 7f 7f 7f 7f 7f

What happens when the processor loads from virtual addresses $\texttt{0x1787}$ and $\texttt{0x2665}$?

  1. Both addresses generate faults.
     
  2. $\texttt{0x1787}$ generates a fault, while $\texttt{0x2665}$ returns $\texttt{0x1A}$.
     
  3. $\texttt{0x1787}$ returns $\texttt{0x1A}$, while $\texttt{0x2665}$ generates a fault.
     
  4. $\texttt{0x1787}$ generates a fault, while $\texttt{0x2665}$ returns $\texttt{0x86}$.

question.text:
Which statement correctly describes the purpose of the valid bit in a page-table entry?

  1. It indicates whether the page has been modified. An invalid-bit access causes the page to be written to disk.
     
  2. It indicates whether the translation may be used by the process. Access through an invalid entry causes the MMU to generate an exception.
     
  3. It indicates whether the page was recently referenced. Access through an invalid entry always produces a TLB hit.
     
  4. It indicates that the page is read-only. Access through an invalid entry is silently ignored.
question.subject: Operating System
